See also: Grammatica and grammàtica

Dutch

[edit]
Dutch Wikipedia has an article on:
grammatica
Wikipedia nl

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin grammatica, from Ancient Greek γραμματική (grammatikḗ, “skilled in writing”), from γράμμα (grámma, “line of writing”), from γράφω (gráphō, “write”), from Proto-Indo-European *gerebh- (“to scratch”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˌɣrɑˈmaː.ti.kaː/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: gram‧ma‧ti‧ca

Noun

[edit]

grammatica f (plural grammatica's, diminutive grammaticaatje n)

  1. grammar (rules for speaking and writing a language)
  2. (metonymic) grammatical manual

Synonyms

[edit]
  • spraakkunst

Derived terms

[edit]
  • basisgrammatica
  • grammaticafout
  • grammaticaregel

Related terms

[edit]
  • grammaticaal
  • grammaticus

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Indonesian: gramatika
  • Negerhollands: grammatica

Interlingua

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

grammatica (plural grammaticas)

  1. grammar

Latin

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • grammatica:
    • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ɡramˈma.tɪ.ka]
    • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ɡramˈmaː.ti.ka]
  • grammaticā:
    • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ɡramˈma.tɪ.kaː]
    • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ɡramˈmaː.ti.ka]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Short for ars grammatica, a partial calque of Ancient Greek γραμματική τέχνη (grammatikḗ tékhnē, “art of letters”), from γραμματικός (grammatikós, “of letters”).

Noun

[edit]

grammatica f (genitive grammaticae); first declension
grammatica n pl (genitive grammaticōrum); second declension

  1. grammar, philology
    Synonym: grammaticē f

Descendants

Adjective
